title: Dow Jones Industrial Average Fast Facts
content: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) is a stock index of 30 ‘blue-chip’ US stocks that gauges the overall strength of the U.S. market. It began in 1896 with 12 industrial stocks; the first index was published on May 26, 1896 at 40.94 points. The first close above 100 came on January 12, 1906 at 100.25. The 1929 crash started on October 24, 1929, and it took 25 years for the Dow to recover its September 1929 high of 381 points. The largest one‑day drop was on October 19, 1987, when the Dow fell 508 points, the biggest single‑day decline at that time. After the September 11 attacks, the Dow fell more than 1,300 points (about 14 %) during the first full week of trading on September 21, 2001. The worst single‑day point drop in history occurred on September 29, 2008, when the Dow plunged 777.68 points, the same day the U.S. House rejected a $700 billion bailout package. The worst weekly decline was from October 6‑10, 2008, when the Dow fell 1,874.19 points (18.15 %). The biggest daily gain was on August 26, 2015, when the Dow closed up 619 points, the largest daily gain since 2008. The worst four‑day percentage loss to start a year was on January 7, 2016, when the Dow dropped 5 %. The Dow’s worst one‑day point drop in history happened on March 16, 2020, when it fell 2,997.1 points and recorded its worst percentage decline since October 19, 1987, an event dubbed ‘Black Monday’.

title: Dow Jones Industrial Average® - Rekordlevel im Fokus
content: The Dow Jones Industrial Average has reached a record level and is now testing the chart-technically significant barriers at 45,074/45,054 points. This level has been a key factor in five of the last seven weeks and a new record high would trigger a new, pro-cyclical buy signal. This is because the trend development of the last 1.5 years can be interpreted as a bullish trend, with a potential long-term follow-up potential of around 8,000 points. The trend line since August 2022 (currently at 48,646 points) is one of the remaining key targets. Support levels are the August low (43,341 points) and the 50-day line (currently at 42,797 points).

title: Así cierra el índice Dow Jones al final del día de hoy, viernes 26 de setiembre de 2025
content: The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 46.31 points on Friday, September 26, 2025, according to data from the Banco República (BROU). This represents a 0.77% increase from the previous closing. The Dow Jones, the principal index of the New York Stock Exchange, tracks the performance of the 30 largest non‑transport and non‑utility companies listed there. Created in 1896, the index has evolved from 12 industrial firms to 20 in 1916 and 30 in 1928, a number it still maintains. Its average price began at 40.94 points, crossed 1,000 in November 1972, and reached 10,000 points in March 1999. The index is calculated by summing the share prices of its constituent companies and dividing by a periodically adjusted divisor, giving higher‑priced stocks greater weight. Investors can gain exposure to the Dow through futures, mutual funds, or ETFs that track the index. The companies represented in the index have historically reflected the U.S. economic profile, shifting from early cotton, sugar, and tobacco firms to today’s finance, oil, technology, communications, aerospace, and retail giants.

title: Dow Jones Industrial Average Primed for Breakout on Weekly Chart | Investing.com
content: The Dow Jones Industrial Average is primed for a breakout on the weekly chart, with a fresh 'buy' trigger on the On-Balance-Volume indicator and a recent 'buy' trigger in the MACD. The index is expected to follow the lead of the S&P 500, which has already cleared its early 2025 high. In contrast, Bitcoin is looking vulnerable to a reversal after failing to push through its breakout on the weekly timeframe. The Nasdaq, on the other hand, has been moving consistently higher on net bullish technicals and is outperforming its peers. The Russell 2000 remains the laggard, but has a net bullish technical picture, while the Semiconductor Index has managed to poke above breakout resistance but finished below it. For this week, the Dow Industrial Average is the preferred choice, with the Semiconductor Index as a solid alternative, and Bitcoin as a potential ancillary benefit.
